case_name: Shaikh Azim @ Vakil @ Kuku v State of Maharashtra
respondent:
State of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

14 July 2008
Criminal Appeal No. 868 of 2007
The Judgment was delivered by : Dr. Arijit Pasayat, J.
1.  Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of the Division Bench of the Bombay High Court, Nagpur Bench, upholding conviction of the appellant for offence punishable under Sections 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the 'IPC') as was awarded by the 9th Additional Sessions Judge, Nagpur. Three persons faced trial. They are Sk. Rahim(A-1), Sk. Azim (A-2) and Sk Ibrahim (A-3). A-1 was acquitted and A-3 was convicted for offence punishable under Section 325 IPC.

facts: The house of Abdul Jabbar Qureshi (hereinafter referred to as the 'deceased') was adjacent to the house of the appellant/accused in Nava Nakasha, Lashkaribagh, Nagpur.
At the relevant time, the appellant along with his two brother i.e. Sk. Rahim and Sk. Ibrahim as well as his parents and grand father were residing in the same house.
The family members of the deceased questioned the conduct of the family members of the accused.
The incident in question took place on 8.8.1986 at about 12.00 noon.
The deceased and his son Abdul Khaliq were present in their house along with other family members.
Accused Sk. Azim (appellant) was holding a Stick, accused Sk. Ibrahim was holding an iron rod and accused Sk. Rahim was also holding a stick in his hand.
Abdul Khaliq received injuries on his person.
The deceased had become unconscious because of the blow which was given by accused no.2, the appellant on the head of the deceased.
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution version is not cogent.
The evidence of PWs. 3 and 6 should not have been relied upon though they claim to have witnessed the incident.
It is submitted that the offence is not covered by Section 302 IPC.
The occurrence took place during the course of a sudden quarrel.
respondent_arguments: All the witnesses have stated that A-2 had assaulted the deceased.
Their evidence does not suffer from any infirmity.
So far as evidence of eye witnesses is concerned, PWs. 1 and 3 were the witnesses of the occurrence.
court_reasoning: The Fourth Exception to Section 300 IPC covers acts done in a sudden fight.
There is provocation in Exception 4 as in Exception 1; but the injury done is not the direct consequence of that provocation.
A 'sudden fight' implies mutual provocation and blows on each side.
It may be that one of them starts it, but if the other had not aggravated it by his own conduct it would not have taken the serious turn it did.
holding: The appeal is allowed to the aforesaid extent.
Custodial sentence of 10 years should meet the ends of justice.
